title: [Direction · v18] Per-user scope for view personal configuration (parked from #7494)
body:
Direction card recording the parked half of the #7494 ruling (maintainer, 2026-08-11 — verbatim authorization in chat: 「接受你的全部建议，请更新 issue 的状态和标签」, accepting the four-lens decision-inbox review in full). Filed by the PM session under the maintainer-directed routing channel.

## What is parked

A true **per-user scope** for view personal configuration (sort / hiddenFields / columnState / rowHeight as genuinely personal overlays), delivering the "Airtable-style per-view personal config" the console prose once promised.

## Why parked, not queued (four-lens)

- **Business pull**: none measured today. The harmful symptoms are closed by the NOW layer of #7494 (permission gate on the org-wide overlay write; honest contract wording) and objectui#4227 (personalization rows distinguishable from saved views; system views not deletable via overlay).
- **Startup focus**: this is a new platform capability surface — a new scope dimension in the view-overlay store, new read/write paths, migration for existing overlay rows. Capability expansion without real demand is exactly what the startup-focus principle defers.
- **Long-term**: per-user scope remains the architecturally right end-state if demand appears; nothing in the NOW layer forecloses it.
- **AI-safety**: the NOW layer already removes the namespace ambiguity that was the active mis-write trap.

## Hold record

- **Date**: 2026-08-11
- **Reason**: no measured customer pull; interim contract (explicit org-wide + permission gate) ships under #7494.
- **Restart condition**: real customer demand for per-user view personalization, or a v18 planning pass over the view/metadata scope model. On restart, re-verify the premises against main first (`git log origin/main --oneline -10 -- packages/metadata* packages/platform-objects` and the objectui adapter `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts`).

## Refs

- #7494 (the ruling this card is split from; NOW layer scope lives there)
- objectui#4155 / objectui#4227 (consumer-side halves)
- objectui PR #4214 (removed the destructive filter-overlay key)
